record.what_it_does: AI meeting recorder that transcribes, summarizes and shares meeting recordings and highlights.
record.auth_notes: Three methods: Personal Access Token (acts as the user), Workspace Access Token (admin-issued), and OAuth2 authorization code with PKCE for integrations other Grain users authorize. Requests also need a Public-Api-Version header. The OAuth app registration process wasn't confirmed because developers.grain.com/authentication returned 403.
record.access_notes: Grain's support page says a PAT is available on every plan, including Free. A WAT needs a workspace admin on Business or Enterprise. No plan requirement is stated for OAuth2. A third-party comparison (Scalekit) claims free plans get no API access, which conflicts with Grain's page. I did not confirm whether OAuth client registration needs approval.
record.api_breadth_notes: v2 REST API at api.grain.com/_/public-api/v2. It covers recordings, highlights, uploads, token-info and hooks. v1 was sunset in September 2026. I didn't count endpoints.
record.mcp_notes: https://api.grain.com/_/mcp (Streamable HTTP). It uses OAuth with dynamic client registration, and a PAT also works. Grain documents it at support.grain.com/en/articles/14811968-how-to-use-the-grain-mcp-server.
record.blocker_notes: Buildable now with a PAT or OAuth2. The caveats are unconfirmed OAuth client registration or review, and conflicting reports on free-plan API access. Composio may already have a Grain toolkit that uses API key auth.

evidence.quote: Create a Personal Access Token (PAT) in your Grain settings under integrations
available on every plan, including Free
Webhooks let Grain push event data to a URL you register in your integration.

record.needs_human: Check whether OAuth2 client registration is self-serve or needs approval, and whether an OpenAPI spec is published. developers.grain.com/authentication returned 403. Also confirm free-plan API access, since Grain's own page says PATs work on Free but a third-party source says otherwise. The MCP URL and the PAT-for-MCP claim come from search-result summaries, not a page I opened. I didn't open the Grain MCP support page itself, so its evidence quote is unverified.
